definitions.explanation: The Fahrenheit temperature scale, used mainly in the United States. Japan uses {摂氏|せっし} (Celsius) for everyday temperatures.

examples.japanese: {華氏|かし}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{表|あらわ}す→表す：01868_arawasu⟧。

examples.english: In America, temperatures are given in Fahrenheit.

examples.japanese: {華氏|かし}⟦{百|ひゃく}→百：00780_hyaku⟧⟦{度|ど}→〜度：09845_do⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{摂氏|せっし}→摂氏：12906_sesshi⟧⟦{約|やく}→約：09563_yaku⟧{三十八|さんじゅうはち}⟦{度|ど}→〜度：09845_do⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{当|あ}たり→当たる：01860_ataru⟧、⟦かなり→かなり：01149_kanari⟧⟦{暑|あつ}い→暑い：00619_atsui⟧。
examples.english: 100 degrees Fahrenheit is about 38 degrees Celsius, which is quite hot.

notes:
{華氏|かし} is the Fahrenheit temperature scale. The character {華|か} was chosen to transcribe the 'Fah' of Fahrenheit's name. Japan normally uses ⟦{摂氏|せっし}→摂氏：12906_sesshi⟧ (Celsius), so {華氏|かし} mostly appears when discussing the US.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {華氏|かし}{〜度|ど}: ~ degrees Fahrenheit
- {華氏|かし}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{測|はか}る→測る：01977_hakaru⟧: to measure in Fahrenheit

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{摂氏|せっし}→摂氏：12906_sesshi⟧: Celsius — the standard scale in Japan
